avoid_supplements.name: High-dose chromium
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive hypoglycemic effects may increase risk of severe hypoglycemia when combined with exenatide's glucose-lowering action
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplemental chromium or use only under medical supervision with increased glucose monitoring

avoid_supplements.name: Fenugreek seeds
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Fenugreek has independent hypoglycemic properties that may potentiate exenatide's glucose-lowering effects
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue fenugreek supplementation or monitor blood glucose closely if use continues

caution_supplements.name: Alpha-lipoic acid
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild additive glucose-lowering effects; risk of hypoglycemia is generally low
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood glucose patterns; inform healthcare provider of concurrent use

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng (American or Asian)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May modestly reduce blood glucose; additive effect possible but typically mild
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of hypoglycemia; dose adjustment of exenatide may be needed

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals
avoid_foods.mechanism: Exenatide delays gastric emptying; high-fat foods further slow gastric transit, increasing GI adverse effects (nausea, vomiting) and reducing medication efficacy
avoid_foods.action: Counsel patient to consume low-fat, balanced meals; avoid fatty or fried foods within 1-2 hours of exenatide administration

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (excessive)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Alcohol impairs hepatic glucose production and increases hypoglycemia risk; exenatide's glucose-lowering effects are potentiated
avoid_foods.action: Avoid alcohol or consume only minimal amounts; increased glucose monitoring required if alcohol is used

caution_foods.name: Large meals
caution_foods.mechanism: Exenatide delays gastric emptying; large portions may worsen nausea and GI discomfort without affecting glucose control significantly
caution_foods.action: Recommend smaller, more frequent meals to improve tolerability

caution_foods.name: Sugary foods and refined carbohydrates
caution_foods.mechanism: These foods may blunt exenatide's therapeutic benefit and increase postprandial glucose excursions in some patients
caution_foods.action: Encourage dietary modification toward complex carbohydrates and whole grains as part of diabetes management

monitoring_notes: Monitor for hypoglycemia, especially when exenatide is combined with insulin or sulfonylureas. Assess gastric tolerance and advise patients on meal composition and timing to optimize both efficacy and tolerability.
